method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21: (1) split the part into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye.

sections.meaning: Retaliation is prescribed, but whoever is pardoned something by his brother, a following up as is right and payment in a good way is a lightening and a mercy; there is life in it.
ideas: A man sets down a heavy stone and offers an open hand to another, a basket of dates on the ground
A man lowers a raised hand and lets it open
Two men on a bridge, one stepping aside to let the other pass

sections.meaning: When death comes, a bequest is made to parents and nearest relatives as is right; whoever changes it after hearing it bears the sin.
ideas: An old man at a table writing, his grown children waiting in the next room
A house key on an envelope beside reading glasses on a table
A sealed letter handed to a young person

sections.meaning: Fasting is prescribed for a limited number of days; for the sick or the traveler other days; God wants ease for you and not difficulty.
ideas: A person sits calmly at a laid breakfast table with an untouched plate as the sun climbs
A table set with bread and fruit seen through a window at sunrise
A steep rocky path beside a gentle winding path, a traveler on the gentle one
A hiker setting down a heavy rucksack and a friend taking the strap

sections.meaning: I am near; I answer the call of the one who calls. The night of the fast: spouses are a garment for one another, and you may eat and drink until the white thread of dawn is clear from the black thread.
ideas: A lone traveler calls into the night and a window lights up very near
A telephone answered on the first ring
A couple wrapped in one shawl on a porch at night
The first thin white line of dawn over dark hills
A white thread and a black thread side by side on a table in dawn light

sections.meaning: Do not eat up your wealth among yourselves by falsehood or bribe the judges; virtue is not coming to houses from the back but by their doors.
ideas: A hand slides an envelope under a judge's bench
A man climbs in through a back window of a house whose front door stands open
A boy climbing over a fence beside an open gate

sections.meaning: Do not overstep the limit; fight only those who fight you; if they stop there is no aggression; spend for good and do not throw yourselves into destruction with your own hands.
ideas: A rope line at a boundary with a man's hand on it
A dam holding back a river
A family comes home carrying bundles to an open door
A man sitting on a branch sawing it off beside the trunk
A man digging a pit beneath his own house

sections.meaning: Complete the pilgrimage and the visit, with supplies, and the best supply is mindfulness; then pour out from Arafat and ask forgiveness.
ideas: A long road with small groups of travelers walking the same way at dawn
A traveler's pack on a table with bread, water and boots
An aerial view of a great crowd pouring across a plain like a river
A river pouring out through a gap in a ridge

sections.meaning: Remember God as you remember your fathers, or more; some ask only for this world and have no share in the hereafter; others ask for good in this world and the hereafter.
ideas: A man counts coins in a dim room while sunrise fills the window unseen
A woman at a window at dawn with both hands cupped open toward the light
A child holding two things at once, an apple and a book

The two men are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.
